uniequip_002_quartz:
'So, what's the plan?'
'Simple: we go into the bar, find our target, and make him tell us where the Originium powder stash is.'
'And the precise timing?' The young girl, having just finished cooking, leans against a pillar in the cellar, carefully wiping down her oversized greatsword.
'Just a powder dealer. Untrained. Don't worry. It'll be a cakewalk.'
'I told you, give me an exact time. That's how every mission should be handled. Or do you plan to come back hungry with no dinner ready?'
'Alright, fine. He'll be there at 7:00 p.m., to meet someone else.'
Quartz finishes cleaning her greatsword and opens a toolkit she'd bought from the town's clockmaker, then starts repairing the pocket watch she'd left on the dining table.
'Thirteen seconds slow,' she says with a sigh.
That evening.
Carrying her greatsword, Quartz pushes open the bar's doors.
In the only place in town worthy of being called entertainment, people were lost in wild revelry. Through the haze of alcohol vapors and clouds of smoke, she spots the target—crouched in the corner, clutching his glass tightly.
She steps over the drunk patrons sprawled on the floor and sits across from him.
'Miss, can I get you a drink?'
'No, thank you. I'm here waiting for someone—7:00, right?'
The target stares intently at her, this strange woman who had unexpectedly started talking to him. Swallowing hard, he suddenly pulls a remote from his bag and shouts:
'You vermin couldn't make it in a nomadic city! And now you're out here in the wasteland, to make my life as miserable as yours! The moment the clock hits 7:00, the Originium powder bomb under this table will blow you sky-high! This is what mercs like you deserve!'
Seven...
The music cuts off abruptly. The revelers freeze in their tracks, turning to look beneath the table where a blurred red countdown clock was flashing.
Six...
The bar's doors fly open, followed by the windows, as those who are still sober drag their unconscious companions out of the building.
'One!' The target shouts, jumping onto the bar and raising his arms as if welcoming a grand finale.
'Sir, your watch is ten seconds fast.'
Quartz lets out a long sigh, raises her greatsword, and brings it down on him.
People watch as a young woman carrying a greatsword hauls a man out of the now-empty bar.
Five seconds later, the bar explodes, sending wood and glass shards soaring, and bursting into a dazzling firework against the night sky.
'Where are you going?'
'To find some cold water to wake him up. Then, to thank my watch repair toolkit.'
uniequip_002_humus:
This is a story from when Humus just came aboard.
Hearing they'd gotten a waste processing station's foreman from the Columbian frontier, several operators from Engineering had their curiosities piqued, wanting to see if someone with that kind of work experience had any special skills.
When Humus checked in at Engineering, carrying his heap of trustworthy tools, clearly used for years, everyone present had quite the scare.
Firstly, the box used to carry them was intimidatingly huge—only someone used to rough work like Humus could carry that thing about by one hand. Secondly, aside from the usual tools was a smorgasbord of bizarrely-shaped wonders whose usages were unclear, enough to perplex anyone who saw them.
Fortunately, Humus is the type who's happy to share. Over the next few hours, Engineering's operators gained a considerable boost to their knowledge.
'This one's a multifunction remote control, with a lot of leeway for remodeling. Just do this... this... reassemble it quickly, and it'll transform from a TV remote to an RC detonator. It's high-power, has a huge effective range, and it's a treat to use.
'This one's basically just an average hand cranked dynamo, but with a little souped-up functionality—it can generate electricity while it threshes corn or maybe peels potatoes. We were constantly out of power at the processing station, after all, and usually we only had corn or potatoes to eat.
'As for this sickle, I made it out of a car door I pulled off. That car was a real funny one—after it came in written off, we had to shelve it for forever because it was just too rugged, and tearing the thing apart took some massive effort. I made the sickle's form overkill enough so if I pull it out and it scares people off, then that's one less pointless fight.'
It so happened that moments after the conclusion of this eye-opening equipment seminar, the bell sounded for dinnertime. Completely dazed, the operators of Engineering were itching to take this out-of-the-ordinary new colleague to the canteen for the welcome party they'd set up in advance. At the table, Humus told his curious coworkers a few stories, of people and things out on the frontier that in his eyes were just everyday life. Yet it was only after his captive audience had finished taking in his stories that they realized why Humus had the skillset that he did.
The frontier's not a place you survive with just the average Joe's common sense.
uniequip_002_wscoot:
After a huge ruckus, the two elders from Gang of Justice reluctantly depart, leaving the place in a mess—wooden chairs smashed over heads, shattered windows broken with bodies, and their iconic wooden sign on the door with 'Yi', or 'justice', written on it, now split into two pieces stuck in the ground.
'Anyone who was injured should head inside to get patched up. Everyone else help me clean up the mess. If any of our customers see this, they're going to be scared away.' Windscoot says this as he takes the lead and grabs a broom with one hand, his other pressing on a cut on his forearm.
'Hey, kid. You're the one who should go get patched up. If you hadn't blocked that blow for me, my head would've been split open.'
'It's just a little cut, I'm not afraid of blood—okay, okay! Enough glaring at me, uncle. I'll go wrap it up once I'm done cleaning.'
The former bandits begin to clumsily clean up the mess. Today their 'escort agency' has far less members than when they were bandits, and the situation seems much more somber after this bout of chaos. Someone picks up the broken 'Yi' and says: 'Are we gonna toss our Justice away just like that?'
Windscoot takes the broken sign and sighs without speaking. The Gang of Justice had broken up, and the escort agency's business was unlikely to improve. Was everything he had done so far the right thing to do?
'Hey,' The uncle jabs at him, 'You did nothing wrong. It was those two who extorted our customers. If they'd carried on with it, it would've been hard for us to continue this line of work.'
'Exactly! I finally learned to read a few words recently too. Wouldn't it all go to waste if our agency goes bankrupt?!'
'And all those super-hard-to-remember passcodes too!'
'Don't get me even started. Those damn traffic rules keep giving me fines round the clock! I won't forgive anyone who makes all my effort go to waste!'
'Haha, isn't that because you're too dumb?'
The crowd chats about the efforts they've put into their new lives, filling the air with laughs. Windscoot unfurrows his brow, and pats his own head, as if trying to expel the hesitation within himself.
The next day, the wooden 'Yi' sign appears again at the escort agency's entrance.
'For now, I just stuck them back together with some nails. I'll make a new one when I have time.' Windscoot returns to his usual cheerful tone.
'Nah, don't bother! This is a pretty unique look. Look at the top and bottom halves—now they're joined even closer than before!'
'Exactly, isn't it the trend these days to have, uh, a logo or whatever? We should trademark it!' Sounds of agreement follow.
'Really? I'll go find someone to turn it into an actual logo then, and print it on our clothes and gear. But remember: you asked for this, so no refusing to wear your future uniforms.'
Windscoot's beaming smile draws a crowd of complaints. Learning to write up orders, practicing martial arts, keeping proper accounts—everyone is busy getting the escort agency on the right track.
uniequip_002_swire:
Swire, Senior Superintendent of the Lungmen Police Department, is off work today, so, just as always, she goes shopping at Paci Plaza.
After a six-hour shopping spree across the entire mall, she is just getting ready to go home with eight big bags in her hands and a big smile on her face. That is, until she turns the corner to a Swire branded lipstick counter.
'The usual. Five #38 Bullets. Thanks,' Swire masterfully asks the salesperson for her favorite lipstick.
The #38 Bullet has been her lipstick of choice for the past ten years. Naturally, the price is of no concern to her.
'Of course, Miss Swire. Right away,' says the salesperson, who seems to be familiar with this process herself. She asks a coworker to take over at the counter and disappears into the storeroom to look for the lipsticks the princess personally requested. Before long, she returns with a wooden carton and hands it over to Swire.
'Please confirm this is the correct amount.'
Without opening the box to check its contents, Swire merely acknowledges the salesperson and looks down to fish for something in her handbag.
After a good while, she takes out a mini bag. To everyone else, this probably looks more like a petite handbag.
She unbuckles her bag, revealing five black velvet slots inside.
In each of those slots is a used up #38 Bullet lipstick.
Swire removes her used lipsticks and places them on the counter before inserting four of her newly purchased lipsticks in the slots, with the fifth one going into her pocket instead.
When she notices Swire placing her bags back on her shoulders again, the salesperson's heart begins to race.
'Miss, would you like someone to help carry your bags?'
'Oh? No need. They are hardly heavy at all.'
'Frightfully sorry, but are you sure...?'
'Yes, I'm sure,' Swire answers as she walks away from the counter. It seems she really needs no help with her bags.
She may not need any help, but there are others who need hers.
Not a moment after she steps out of the shopping mall's front doors, Swire hears a loud scream for help. She turns to the scream's direction to find a thief dashing away with a woman's handbag in his hands.
It so happens she is running right toward a superintendent of the L.G.D.
'What a coincidence,' Swire thinks to herself.
By chance, she does not have her flail with her.
It so happens she just bought new lipstick today.
What's more, there is one right in her pocket right now.
She decides to teach the thief a lesson he will never forget.
Swire sets her shopping bags down, takes out her lipstick and removes the cap, breaking the seal, and waits for the thief to come closer.
A few seconds later, everyone in the vicinity hears a thud, followed by the thief's wail as he stumbles to the ground under the L.G.D. patrol officer's roar.

Several minutes later...
'Good work, Missy. You're off duty, and you still caught a thief for us.' Hoshiguma, here to oversee the arrest of the thief, forces a smile as she greets Swire, the brave good Samaritan.
Normally, Swire would personally take the man in herself for interrogation.
However, she has the day off. This case isn't hers to deal with.
'This fellow has got to have some real rotten luck to run into me today.'
'It's not every day someone bumps into an off duty inspector when they go to snatch something.'
'Hmph, whatever. You take him in. I'm going home. I'll deal with the case tomorrow.'
'If you say so, Missy.'
'Before you go, I have a question for you.'
'What is it?'
Swire turns around to find Hoshiguma writing something on her case report.
'What should I write for how the suspect was taken down?'
Swire can tell that Hoshiguma is asking for her opinion.
'Just write down that it was lipstick. There is no need to pull punches for someone like him.'
'Ahaha, okay then,' says Hoshiguma as she cheerfully scribbles on her report, 'The suspect was taken down by lipstick.'
'I don't even want to head straight home anymore. Why don't you hurry and finish up with work? We'll get dinner together.'
'Would you like me to escort you home and carry your bags for you, Missy? Haha.'
'Oh, enough questions. Hurry up already.'
'Okay, give me a second. I'll give the report to somebody else, then we can get dinner.'
'Be sure to tell me how amazing this lipstick of yours is.'
'Certainly.'

'Why don't you carry my bags for me now? My hands are getting sore.'
'Okay, okay. Be right with you.
uniequip_002_sophia:
Even before the match, Zofia knew that she had a long way to go if she were to defeat the Fissure Knight, but it wasn't until she actually had to fight the Fissure Knight that she knew how fatal the gap between them was.
She heard that her opponent had staff who reviewed all of her previous matches and had been trained by coaches bearing the same weapon and comparable stature to her. In effect, her opponent already knows her like the back of his own hand.
She had also heard that the Fissure's armor was forged specifically to take on her weapon of choice in battle. Not only does this armor make it difficult for her to get a good grasp with her whislash, any attack she manages to land isn't going to hurt her opponent in any way.
On the other hand, the blades yielded by her opponent have both been treated to give them fine cutting abilities.
She used to think these were just rumors. Alas, it all turned out to be true.
Zofia is starting to get discouraged. After all, her last few matches have all resulted in her defeat.
How many companies are there sponsoring Fissure? Are there really tens of thousands of people racking their brains together just to figure out how to take on the Whislash Knight?
She needs to find a way to get herself out of this, lest she gets defeated yet again.
Did Nearl use to fight all by herself as she is doing now?
Did she waver and hesitate when she found herself at a disadvantage?
She knows the answer, and she also knows very well that she is not Nearl.
When her techniques, weapons, and armor are unable to give her any advantages, the only things she has to rely on are the same things that led Nearl to victory.
Conviction and determination.
She starts switching up her attack patterns, even using techniques that she has not yet completely mastered.
She's relying more on her blade than her whislash to attack.
Now, Zofia the Whislash has a clear objective:
She must confuse her opponent.
She must wait for her opponent to become distracted for even a second.
She must snatch his weapon away with her whislash.
And before its threads snap, she must strike her opponent down!
uniequip_002_bryota:
Old posters, cassette tapes, graphite pencils, ballpoint pens, coloring books, swimming goggles... Miscellanies are tossed one after another onto the bed. The young boy seems to be looking for an important treasure, hence his excursion through his big brother's 'secret base.'
'Look what I found! Liv, you gotta look!'
The young girl comes running at the call, and seeing the topsy-turvy state of the room, somewhat angrily pouts.
'Lut! You... Harley said not to mess with Enis's stuff!'
'*clatter*! It's the schedule for Enis's part-time job—
'Don't you wanna know where he went today, and what he's doing now?'
'......'
The boy waves about his brother's schedule, brandishing it like it's a spoil of war. The girl follows with big round eyes, watching fixedly as the sheet flutters through the air. She's totally won over, the errands the grown-ups gave her gone in a puff of smoke.
'Enis said he'd play kick the can with me!'
'Enis said he'd braid my hair for me!'
And so, one sprawled on the bed and the other leaning by the wall, the two little rascals vie over it, each wanting the bigger slice of their brother's time.
'5:30, restock, there is no pepper, if you do not buy it Harley will think the food tastes like nothing again.'
'9:30, deliver letters, also mail Chuck the trekking sticks he wants, they are just picking up dust at home.'
1 to 4, Grandpa Tom's sunbathing time, look after store for him. Save ice cream for Liv and Lut, strawberry and chocolate!'
'At 6...'
'At 8...'
The day was packed, and the to-do list was too. The little ones looked and pondered, and it seemed there was no free time to squeeze in anything else.
'Oh, with so much to do... will Enis make it back for dinner?'
'He'll definitely come back for dinner! Instead of going for ice cream, let's help Harley with dinner...'
'So, no more kick the can?'
'No more hair braiding!'
The little boy pulled out a chessboard from under the bed, and the little girl found the chess pieces in a drawer.
'After dinner, we can play this!'
'But Enis has been working all day; he must be really tired... Will he still play with us?'
'Of course! Enis says...
'He loves playing with us the most!'
uniequip_002_rdoc:
'I thank you for saving him. We would be glad to pay you, but... we cannot bring you with us.'
So elaborates an elderly Feline woman, sat in the shade of a wagon's canopy. Beside her lies a light and dirtied mattress, upon which a Lupo man about her age writhes, limbs as if tied in knots. But his face is peaceful enough, and his sweat has more or less subsided—effects of the medicine.
'Don't worry, I promise I won't hold you up. I may even be able to help you further.'
A tan-skinned middle-aged man continues to try and persuade him. He has no obvious racial characteristics, rendering him slightly mysterious.
'Look, we get disasters on this route all the time. That's why it's all us old folks running it. Why should you have to risk it?'
'There's a Catastrophe Messenger in town; I have a map he drew. Your destination should be within comms range of that city. If this is about safety, then all the more reason I should come with you.'
'We... but we only have enough water and rations for ourselves. We don't mean to be stingy, but when supplies are this scarce we can't afford another mouth...'
'I have my own provisions. We just need to follow the route on the map, and you won't run out of food or water. Add in my supplies, and we'll have even more flexibility.'
'This old wagon of ours only sits two at the front. We couldn't possibly trouble you.'
'I can sit with the cargo, I've no problem with that.'
'Well—we'll unload as soon as we get there and there's nothing for us to haul back. If we leave first, you won't have a ride back to Siracusa for quite a while.'
'Doesn't matter, I'll rendezvous with my friends in the city... I just insist on finding my way there alone, that's all. I know you mean well, madam, but you don't need to worry for me. I'm just as concerned for the two of you. Your health, I mean.'
'......
'*sigh*
'I know what you're going for. We do see people like you now and then. But that city's people want for everything, and just the little we send them hardly even makes a difference sometimes. You'll see as much if you go; with bad luck, you'll die there yourself... In the end, whether it's the city folk or us outside, we're all good people living tough lives.
'We're old. We're used to it. But why should you have to?'
Gustave Kateb lifts his head and gazes in the direction he's bound for. He cannot see anything resembling a road, and though he hears that it's a gargantuan structure that spits earth, smoke, and dust and is assembled from an array of nomadic plates, no city has yet entered his vision. Only the haze of sand and ash on the horizon, reflected in eyes of the same shade.
'You're not wrong. I still know far too little about this place, and my past experience won't always apply. Even if I'm prepared physically, I have no basis to claim I'm ready mentally.
'But time is short, and there's too much to do. Overthinking this gets me nowhere. So stop trying to talk me out of it and let's go.'
The city's name is Kazdel. To him, the place is completely unfamiliar. Even its name cannot be found in the land of his birth.
But that does not matter. He is a doctor. Whether at home or afar, he is always pressed to go to wherever needs him most.
uniequip_002_franka:
Tenth routine physical examination.
Oripathy prognosis is stable, Originium Arts have improved due to disease progression, and the new Arts Unit prepared beforehand has been loaded. Subsequently, thermite blade's power will be greatly increased.
Well, huh... Looking at things this way, Originium only sucks when it acts up and hurts a lot. But other than that, it doesn't get in the way of my life, and can even help me in battle. Isn't that pretty decent?
Hmm, maybe that's what I'll tell the teacher’s pet the next time I see her. Can't wait to see what kind of face she makes.
Wonder how she'd even respond to that...
'Your health isn't some kind of game!'
'What's so decent about that? You're actually going to die!'
Sheesh, what's the big deal anyway? You only live once, right? So why not enjoy it?
'Didn't you say you wanted to go traveling across the world? With Oripathy...'
......
......
Yeah, about that travel planner...
I'm not gonna get to check off a lot of things from my bucket list.
It sucks that I didn't even make it through a tenth of my list before getting sick. And some of the places still on it don't welcome the Infected at all. The vast tundras of Ursus, Londinium's eclectic manors, Leithanien's concert halls, Kazimierz's knight tournament arenas, the thousands of fowlbeasts sweeping across Sargon's deserts...
I wanted to see all of them, with her.
Might as well cross them out now...
Jeez, why am I thinking about all these things anyway... It's all because of that teacher’s pet. I listen to her nagging too much. Even when she's not here, I hear her voice in my head.
Stop thinking about these things.
......
Let's keep those plans after all.
Rhodes Island is still moving forward, so I have to keep moving forward.
Maybe one day...
Just maybe, those places will open their doors to welcome the Infected.
uniequip_002_flameb:
This blade, and its master, once had the opportunity to end his life. Yet in the end, this blade ended up shattered.
One piece remains buried in the mud of that battlefield, and the other piece rests on the flowerbed's frame.
'That guy came with a score to settle.'
'That standard-issue longsword looked like a merc weapon.'
'Said he was getting revenge for a friend, but I had no idea who he was talking about.'
'The branches in this pot have already begun to turn yellow, and it'll be difficult for it to sprout new ones'
'What can one do when one’s lost one’s will to live?'
'Putting someone else's life above his own, a meaningless gesture.'
'Utterly ridiculous.'
'People always talk about how they're willing to get run through for their friends. You hear it a lot.'
'But when it comes to how many can actually live up to the talk... Hah, guess he's pretty impressive.'
'Ugh... the two branches here have tangled together and are starting to wilt. Going to have to prune them'
'When you prune them and let them bud again, the part that survives flourishes. Even plants are like that.'
'Too bad he didn't know how to swing a sword at all. Nothing but brute strength.'
'Even after I broke his blade, he still wanted to complete his revenge, literally tooth and nail.'
'He left his life behind so that the living could pay the price.'
'A somewhat interesting idea, but...'
'You'll never become strong if you only see your life as an extension of the dead.'
'When plants treat the offshoots that have been pruned and propagated as their own nutrition, they will flourish more vigorously, and perhaps even bloom more flowers.'
'All life is like this.'
'......'
'This pot might not do too well in the greenhouse. Go take it to the balcony.'
'Maybe it'll grow into something new.'
uniequip_002_morgan:
Something's definitely new about the Slobberknocker's sign.
Back in the gym in the lockdown zone, Morgan's first order of business is to check the sign hung over the entrance, with Vina's blessing. The shoddy paint has bubbles trapped in it, and the big 'Slobberknocker' that's been carved is definitely a cleaner job than when Hannah first had a go.
Inside the big lockbox under Morgan's bed rest her dearly beloved Morgan's Memoirs, still safe and sound. After triple-checking it hasn't been touched at any point, she pulls out the good tipple stashed alongside, takes two honking swigs, then chokes and starts hacking and coughing.
Past its best-by date, but still. If it was a good tipple, it's always worth a try.
Now fretful, Morgan looks through the pile of old cruft in her box. Something's missing.
But it turns out to be a page that's fallen out of her Memoirs, and just a quick skim is enough for her to remember all the details.
This was back when their old neighborhood friends weren't taking the Glasgow Gang's biz seriously yet. No denying that Morgan's ideas then were absolute rotters from time to time, stuff like getting outsiders to buff up the gang's standing. Who knew she and the one-track mind Hannah would hit it off so easily? And so they went about harassing plenty of youths from Victoria's other parts.
Until Hannah was humiliated at the hands of she who protected those youths, Vina.
That was the first time Morgan heard Vina's name, more than a decade ago. Hannah just kept pestering Morgan to talk this 'outsider' Feline into joining the gang. Went as far as talking about 'protecting the neighborhood toy factory' and stuff like that as a front. Shame the Feline in question wouldn't fall for that.
What narked Hannah more was when some noble's servant from the city center came to mess with the toy factory for whatever reason, both she and Morgan tried to stick their heads out for the neighborhood and took a horrid beating instead. And then in the end, who but Vina would show up and shoo the two out of there.
Hannah came back and spent that entire afternoon in a huff. After making a big show to Vina that blew up in their faces, she'd never agree to join now. But to the surprise of both, that night a Vina covered in wounds ran up to the gym cradling a huge box of local specialty toys, banging away on the door.
'From the toy factory's owner. This way everyone'll know the factory is under Glasgow Gang protection.'
Morgan made fun of Hannah about it for ages afterwards. The dumbstruck Hannah and the visibly impassioned Vina would become the principal heroes of the Memoirs in time.
And it's ever since then that Morgan's decided deep down to protect Vina. After all, everyone knows the poncey lords doomed themselves by messing with Central.
It's there that Vina, wearing a perplexed face and holding a rusted toy, interrupts Morgan's reminiscence.
'I found this in my room. Do you remember whose it is?'
Morgan finally twigs what was missing from the box. Up in high spirits, she slings her arm over Vina's shoulders.
'Let's go ask Hannah. She might know.'
At least nobody's changed.
uniequip_002_laios:
All along his search for Rhodes Island, Laios has been quietly gathering odds and ends in anticipation of his return to the dungeon, where he might continue studying their wonders.

INTIMIDATION POSES. A set of hand-drawn how-tos by Laios for use in combat, one for the mock-gloompincer (imitate mandibles with the arms as a deterrent) and one for the mock-Originium slug (arch the body and imitate pricking with the hands). The gloompincer chart also has a small annotation to the side: 'could be interpreted by male gloompincers as a mating ritual.'
SKETCH OF MON3TR. Multiple hand-drawn sketches of Mon3tr from different angles by Laios. Finely rendered, but the abdomen and claws are given a jarring level of detail, possibly suggesting he had the chance to observe up close while being grabbed by Mon3tr. Small annotation to the side: 'so cool!'
A FEATHER. Confirmed by Zumama to be from the High Priest, who has filed with Rhodes Island for a restraining order. Nevertheless, countless operators report seeing the High Priest waiting in areas Laios frequents, and even perching on his head. HR operators suspect the High Priest may actually be enjoying the attention.
SEEDS. Sami silencing chestnut seeds (P.S. works on Marcille), Rim Billitonian bottletree fruit (P.S. is swimming in the tree trunk possible?), Iberian seagrass roots (P.S. tongue numb after taste), etc. Doodle on a note to the side of a walking mushroom, with... the head of an Originium slug?
SEA TERROR IN A BOTTLE. A small Sea Terror kept in a bottle. Laios occasionally feeds it different things to test what it eats, and observes how it is able to change form in such a short time. Unfortunately, this one hasn't demonstrated even the slightest metamorphosis, which has more than saddened Laios.

Laios had a spot in his armor where he could nestle these items safe and sound, but in a tragic turn of events, Marcille spotted his Sea Terror during feeding time, and then everything else too, ending in the forcible disposal of the entire bundle by her hands.
Operators at the scene report that Laios was 'like a hoarding musbeast who had a year's worth of food soaked by rain,' and simply walked away down the corridor with his head hung low. He contacted HR and relayed the day's events out of concern for the repercussions, following which we discovered the Sea Terror in a standard wastebin in an ordinary Rhodes Island hallway.
Pursuant to this, HR has elected to commend Marcille for her safety awareness, and to act on an immediate and pressing need to put Laios through safety training.
uniequip_002_tiger:
Keep a steady form, and control your pace. This is what the leader of Norport Borough's gang would tell herself. Indra could barely keep herself conscious, but she used all her will to keep herself together and face the enemy head-on. Here, at the decisive moment, all she ought to need was one more jab.
'You still want to go?' The calm voice of the opposing party was nearly drowned out by the sound of her own heavy gasps for air.
Loose silver hairs drooped down across her forehead, blocking her vision and blurring out the golden figure standing firm before her, illuminated by a streetlamp. 'Don't be so quick to call yourself the winner, you little shite! I ain't lost yet!' Indra adjusts her breathing and secretly shifts her center of gravity to behind her left hip, all while gathering her hair firmly behind her shoulders. She raises her fists and clenches her fingers, gripping her shabby brass knuckles even tighter than ever before.
'I'll help you remember, outsider. This here street's mine—Indra of the Glasgow Gang!' As soon as the words were out of her mouth, the silver figure suddenly steps forward, pouncing upon her opponent faster than the eye could see. She lifts her left fist as if putting every last ounce of strength into this one strike, but then commands her body to turn and instead funnel all that strength into her right fist.
Indra hears the golden-haired girl mutter in her ear: 'I'll remember alright, Indra of the Glasgow Gang.' A tranquil voice, as she always was. Indra still remembers that after, she lost her balance, she fully expected the cold embrace of the cement road, but that hard sensation looming large in her imagination never came. Through closed eyes, it was like she had... fallen onto a ball of sunshine.
'Run? Run from what? Sorry Vina, I was daydreaming a bit, didn't hear ya.'
'How to Fight with the Glasgow Gang. This was your work, wasn't it? Rule Number Four, and this is the most important rule: When it comes time to run, remember to run.'
'Ah, yeah! Pretty much sums up every street fight I've gotten into over the years.'
'That night we first met, why didn't you run?'
'Gonna have to have a think on that one.' Indra lowers her head and contemplates for a moment. 'Back then, whenever we ran from a fight, it was so we could survive. For scroungers on the street, nothing's more important'n staying alive. But...'
'But?' Siege sits up, facing herself towards Indra.
Indra raises her head, looking right back at Siege. Under the flickering lights of the boxing gym, two pairs of golden eyes face each other, and she sees herself reflected in the Aslan's eyes.
'But there's no Feline who doesn't like some time under the sun, right?' Indra draws back the corners of her mouth, impishly baring an ivory grin.
uniequip_002_flint:
Soon to return to Acahualla, Kemar takes her flashcards with her. The handwriting's kind of immature, and she doesn't need them to remember what the words mean now, but still she hooks them on her belt, the well-worn eyelet fraying day by day.
'These ones, I brought from home. The rest, I picked on the outside,' replied Kemar once upon a time, when a Rhodes operator was curious about the flowers on her cards. At first, they were how the girl of the rainforest learned her way through other languages—they fascinated her since she was young. Tender little plants. As enrapturing as a flying fist, and they called to her the way the wild things did.
On a certain level, these flowers held more strength than any brave warrior. Their names and stories were some of the earliest things Kemar knew by heart: learning how the people beyond the rainforest colored the four seasons with them, interpreted their lives with them. What describes these flowers now are no longer unfamiliar words, but a ring of keys, hung on her waist, opening each of Terra's doors alongside her.
'Look well, it's our tribe's tallest, mightiest warrior! Her footprints are left in places even our imaginations couldn't reach! And now, she's back!' Kemar parts the grass weave over the doorway, and is met head on with the eager chatter of her tribesfolk, in her native language. Eventually, she stirs; in this most familiar of rainforests, she'll never be needing any 'key'.
The tribe's kiddies mill around Kemar, jabbing zealously at all the names on her flashcards' flowers, pestering her to tell all her stories from beyond the forest.
'Beyond the rainforest... it's very wide.'
Kemar recalls the most exciting moment of her own language-learning. Not the first time she understood a spoken word. Not being able to fluently converse with Big Boss Blaze. It was when she realized she could finally explain to others, coherently and clearly, the things that all the flowers of her home represented.
'...But don't let me tell you about it. You should all go see it for yourself!
'And then face off with the people outside, and tell them... let them know how mighty we are.' Kemar flips back to the very first flashcard, pressed with a flower of the rainforest. Its power to live is unwavering, and its power to adapt is unrivalled. Rainforest, prairie, or barrens, it will bloom more avidly, more ardently than all.
uniequip_002_dagda:
This round shield sent from Rhodes Island's Engineering Department seems rather plain, but robust and reliable. Apparently it was the result of the Department holding a 'traditional Victorian arms manufacturing competition' in their spare time. 'This was one of the symbols of a knight,' said the Engineering operator to Dagda in their most charming voice, 'so we decided it'd be best to give it to one of the lady knights making the rounds between Rhodes Island and Victoria.' Dagda looks at the shield proudly displayed atop the table, and can't help but think back to the time before she was accepted as a trainee under the Knights of the Tower.
Back then, other than the strict physical and tactical training regimens, she also took many classes on knightly etiquette. Amongst the grueling and complicated tests of memory and body language drills, this simple round shield had been a major component of them. The historical piece of military equipment was once used daily by knights of old, but the knights of today have long since left theirs at home when marching to war. They would be hung above fireplaces, or used as a nameplate to display one's identity. Expensive paints were commonly used to draw family crests or the coats of arms of various knightly orders. These brightly-colored designs would cover up the shield's own color, just as their delicate etiquette would cover up the inherent violence a knight represents.
Finn, the Captain of the Watch, once described a scene of the knights and their dazzling shields to Dagda: During the evenings of celebration days, the knights would parade down the street, clad in fine armor and with arms in hand. Their shields with their crests and blazons would proudly display images of their birthplaces, or warriors in various stances, or myriad different flowers, or great sturdy beasts, or checkered patterns one could weave into a net. The crisp rhythm of the military drums accompanied deep horns enveloping the orderly knights, and by the end of the parade they would all face towards the flame atop the tower. But that tower has long since collapsed, and these knightly tableaus now exist only in Dagda's imagination.
'I've never actually seen the scene my mentor once described to me.' Recovering her senses somewhat, Dagda continues. 'Just like those books that record the exploits of knights long past, and the ones attempting to define whether a knight's life was glorious and honorable, my position as a knight is long gone. If you asked me if there's still anything worth engraving on that...' Dagda takes the shield off to the workshop, where she draws what she considers to be her emblem—a coat of arms from the streets.
uniequip_002_whitew:
The smith thought long and hard before crafting the weapon.
The head of Famiglia Saluzzo had approached in person, requesting a unique weapon for his daughter.
He accepted the commission not only out of respect for the famiglia's influence—
The swordsmith from Higashi believed that a blade reflects one's soul, and to wield one is to grasp one's destiny.
He once forged a nodachi requiring the strength of five men; of course, the samurai who wielded it was invincible on the battlefield, yet was plagued by injuries in his old age, eventually taking his own life due to that festering anger towards himself.
He once forged a splendorous and dignified blade concealing a razor edge for a rare king. The weapon granted the king an aura of gravitas that permeated the land, and the king never had to wield it against any enemy throughout his entire life.
He once wished to demonstrate his loyalty to Signora Sicilia like the others, yet was rejected nonchalantly. It was then he came to understand how she ruled this country replete with violence, as well as the weariness and helplessness she hid.
But now, he had no idea what sort of fangs this strange young wolf should bear.
An exquisite rapier, because she would inherit her father's eccentricity and elusiveness?
A deadly great-axe, because she could not ignore the call of the wild in her blood?
No, neither would suffice. The smith tossed the half-finished weapon into the furnace's flames.
She was cruel, elegant and elusive as her father, yet something altogether different.
'It's still not ready? My dear father did say to wait until my coming-of-age ceremony, but our enemies wish to see it tonight.'
The swordsmith explained that he was trying to forge a blade worthy of her. But the more he racked his brain, the harder it became to imagine what such a weapon would actually look like.
'How about these?'
She haphazardly picked up a pair of swords.
Once upon a time, he had hoped to create a weapon that would serve as a testament to his skill. This pair of swords had demanded too much of his ingenuity, becoming more and more complex in the process. They sufficed as a conduit for Arts, but had become terribly unwieldy in the process, unable to even be sheathed.
'A failure, destined to never be completed?' The white wolf waved the blades around and bared a smile—'I think I like the sound of that.'
The smith pleaded that her unique soul deserved a weapon far more special.
'I'm afraid you have the wrong idea, sir. What I came here for was a tool. These are sturdy, and more than suitable to kill with. I like the craftsmanship, and plan to keep using them. That's good enough for me.'
The despairing smith could do nothing but watch her leave.
Perhaps, his finest work was something he had rejected as a failure.
Perhaps, any soul that could be defined by a weapon was too empty to begin with.
That night, the renowned swordsmith announced his retirement, and Lappland of Famiglia Saluzzo wielded her iconic blades for the first time—
From that day on, the people would call them 'The Young Fang.'
uniequip_002_ayer:
Portable Wildland Stimulant: Preparation, Instruction and Efficacy
[Preparation and Instruction]
1. Prepare some cooked edamame. Do not salt or peel them.
2. Prepare a device to freeze the edamame. I will use my own edamame box here as a demonstration: this much freezing is just right.
3. Prepare a device to discharge electricity. I'll demonstrate with my trusty sidekick here: this much power leakage is just right.
4. Lower the voltage of the discharge device and shock the edamame until the juice inside carries a slight charge.
5. Eat.
[Efficacy]
In the barrens, maintaining a clear mind can be a real challenge. The boundless wilderness, the sweeping dust storms, the glow reflecting from the active Originium clouds in the sky, the howl of the wind blowing through Originium crystal clusters... It's easy to gradually lose your sense of self and fall into a trance-like state where you won't notice incoming dangers.
Chew the edamame along with its shell. The hairs of the shell can stimulate the mouth, thus keeping the user's nerves active.
Frozen edamame can stimulate the gums and make it easier to stay awake.
The slightly-charged juices can give a tingling jolt, thus sharpening the user's perception.
Proper stimulation can prevent people from falling into a stupor. This is the only way to survive in the wilderness.

'You've put a weird amount of thought into this manual, Ayers.'
'Quit flapping your gums, Leon. A lot of operators have been coming by the last few days, asking me for the secret to staying awake in the wilds. I'm sick of giving the same explanation again and again.'
'I guess it's true that your manual could stop people from coming, but... to be honest, I'm surprised those hobbies of yours can actually come in handy.'
'That's a nice bonus. Edamame is delicious, and I find the electric jolt refreshing.'
'Well, whatever floats your boat. At first, I was worried you were forcing yourself to do all that just to stay awake protecting me...'
'Do I seem like that kind of person?'
'Not really. Remember the first time you ate edamame? With shell and everything? You didn't know to peel it back then and we were worried it'd cause some sort of problem, but instead you seemed happy as could be.'
'I remember. That was when the mining ship broke down in the barrens. By the time we got it huffing and puffing to the next mine, everyone was already delirious with hunger. It was the first time I had food that could just snap you back to your senses, and it really stuck with me.'
'Wait, so it all comes back to waking you up after all? You know, I'm starting to feel a little sorry for you, Ayers.'
'No, it's because edamame is delicious, and I find the electric jolt refreshing.'
'...Alright then. Whatever floats your boat.'
uniequip_002_leto:
At first, not everyone got along particularly well.
That pretty much goes without saying.
Lada would silently hide behind Sonya. Anna wasn't any better; though she was clearly trying to keep her emotions in check, I could tell that she was panicking. Sonya felt like she had a duty to protect the others, so she kept her hand tightly gripped around her axe. I always thought her hand was going to slip one of these days.
Under that atmosphere, everyone was constantly on edge. And to make matters worse, nobody knew if what we were doing was right or wrong.
Lada wanted to be of help—she felt like she was always sheltered by Sonya, and was afraid of being left behind—so she'd go out and try to find us something to eat, though she came back with empty hands most of the times. Anna wanted the group to be more 'stable,' so she'd try to strike up conversations, but they seldom went the way she wanted. Sonya was generally in high spirits, but every so often she'd come back with an extra wound or two.
Everyone did their best to get something done, as if they'd go mad if they didn't. Though sometimes, you could get rid of the 'as if' part.
As for me, I was never that scared in the first place, but it's not like I'd have been happy dying there. I didn't want to lose Sonya and the others either—we'd been friends already. So, I also did whatever I could: bringing back supplies, helping Sonya 'take out the trash,' and even teaching some harsh lessons to anyone who tried to lay their hands on Anna.
At first I thought things would get better, but it was actually the opposite. Lada and Anna started avoiding eye contact with me, and even Sonya would strangely glare at me. That's when I understood: I'd been robbing them of their agency.
But I was better at those things, so why shouldn't I do it?
Of course, I was never the petty type, and it's not like Lada or Sonya really blamed me for that. I knew they were both real nice, we just didn't know how to get along back then. It wasn't until the day Sonya came back from a scuffle with a serious tear in her uniform and Anna used a sewing kit I'd scavenged to fix it up that I realized what I needed to do.
I snuck into the warehouse, found some coats, and brought them to Anna to ask her if she could fix them up into something more cold-resistant. We'd need them later when the weather turned cold, and sure enough, she cheered up at that.
After that, I risked my hide to steal some Reunion kitchenware for Lada so it'd be easier for her to cook, though obviously it was better to keep that part low-key. Her eyes lit up the instant she saw what I brought back.
I even found some self-defense equipment for everyone, and modified them with Sonya. While we were working together, I thumped my chest and said to her: If there's anything you want, just say the word and I'll get it for you. Sonya stared at me for a while, but this time, she nodded.
Looking back now, it was probably around then that our team actually started taking shape.
uniequip_002_chimes:
'These are the only remaining towns and villages in the mountains. I've marked them on the map. Generally, you can just follow the indicated order when delivering mail. I've used different colors to mark each section; each corresponds to different road conditions and recommended modes of transportation—just a bit of advice from someone who's been doing this a while.
'First, there's the part with the smoothest roads, where you can ride a bike. Going downhill is exhilarating, but mind your speed. No matter how good the mountain roads are, they're still bumpy; if your package gets jostled too much, it could fall apart. It'd be almost impossible to find a letter and retrieve it if you lose it in the mountains, so be careful.
'Next is the section you'll have to cover on foot. Walking mountain paths isn't easy, but the most important thing is to race against the weather. You'll need to read the skies. When clouds gather, you should walk faster; when it darkens, you should start running. When it thunders, it'll be already too late to think about finding shelter. Traveling in the rain can be dangerous. My horn, err... I learned this the hard way. As for wild beasts or bandits, stay calm. It's no big deal. I can handle them, and if you're taking over my route, you can too.
'Finally, there are some special paths that are rarely used—I'm running out of space, so I'll write the rest on a separate sheet. But I'll mention one here: the zip lines. Don't be afraid; I've ridden them many times. They're safe, even pleasant. You might come to enjoy them after a while.'
...
'Oh, and one last thing I should write here—it's a small favor. There are a few villages with hardly any young folks left, and I marked them on the map. The elders there tend to be a bit stubborn, and some aren't very mobile, so please be patient and lend a hand if you can. I thank you on their behalf. Truly.
'I almost forgot the most important part: make sure to protect yourself against Oripathy! Don't let the...'
The writing stops abruptly on the back of the map, filling every inch of the small piece of paper. Wind Chimes had left it there after returning from a checkup at the doctor's. Much time has passed since then, and Wind Chimes continued to walk those mountain paths year after year, but the old map remained lying on her desk. One day, someone happened to flip it over and couldn't help but give a wry smile.
'This girl's so naive—she really hoped someone else would be willing to deliver mail all the way up to those remote mountain villages, just like she does.'
'I'd say when the people are all gone, there won't be any need for another Messenger anyway.'
'(Sigh) It's been so many years, and there are so many stories on these roads; no letters could capture them all.'
'And the road is so long... no messenger could ever walk it all.'
uniequip_002_bibeak:
Bibeak knows the heart going into each little stitch.
From the very first lines sketched on graph paper, to a custom order of cloth after talking it over and over with the shop owner, it's all as a gift to herself.
Its future gradually taking shape in Bibeak's hands, a clear forecast of the brilliant piece it'll become.

Life aboard Rhodes Island is freer than you'd imagine. Even though she came on to take treatment and aid, she can still take up the yarn as she likes. She's even started a cozy little class in the sewing room, teaching children who look forward to the future just as she does.
It was all curious and new for the first-time visitors. They squeezed about, reaching out to touch all the tools on the tables—a boy amongst them knocked a fabric cutter away by accident, making a slice in the cloth.
It panicked the children so suddenly, and without thinking they started to push at the perpetrator, who was even more frightened himself.
'You messed up Miss Bibeak's clothes!'
'Miss Bibeak! He did it!'
Bibeak saw the damaged cloth, but didn't even have the chance to speak before the boy, now bright red, fled the room.
Once Bibeak assuaged the children, she inquired where he might've gone, and after a knock and an 'Are you there?', the teary-faced boy came out of the door to his room. His head was hung low, and he held out his savings bank.
'I put all my pocket money in this burdy bank! I'm really, really sorry for ruining your clothes, Miss Bibeak!'
Just as all teachers should, Bibeak knelt down and softly patted him on the shoulder to console him, and the sobs from the crybaby in her embrace gradually ceased.

There's always far too much in life that runs contrary to your expectations, just like how Bibeak doesn't know what kind of design her pencil will put to paper in the coming seconds. Will it gild the lily, so to speak? Or will it change everything about what it was?
She accepts the savings bank, but does not break it open. She prepares to revise the style of clothing, planning to sew a shirt fit for a grown child to wear.
Ordinary tailors would amend an unwitting mistake, but a good tailor allows it to transform into a happy accident, one nobody sees coming.
When the children come to the sewing room for classes again, the boy who blundered last time has his head low, standing at the very back.
With a smile, Bibeak pulls him up to the table, and takes out the all-new shirt: 'I've accepted your burdy bank. Let everyone take a look, now—these are clothes made for you.'
The children erupt in cheers, and they shove on the lucky little boy, clearly even more excited himself.
His cheeks are aglow, and Bibeak knows, he'll surely cherish this present, and when he puts it on afterwards, he'll go do the right thing.
That's what a tailor dreams of, using needle and thread to sew fine futures and bring them to others.
Putting wishes and hopes into dress, for every person to wear.
uniequip_002_tachak:
On Rhodes Island's top deck, a warrior and a girl look out to the sun that's slowly disappearing beneath the horizon.
'Mr. Alexsandr...'
'Were you... a soldier?'
'I'm still a soldier.'
'What's your motherland like?'
'It's a beautiful place.'
The old soldier looks into the distance and describes what his homeland is like to the girl standing next to him.
From the riverscapes of the Volga to the majestic sights of Mamayev Kurgan.
None of them exist in this world.
'Do you love that place?'
'I love it all with all my heart.'
'And you?'
'I lost everything in Chernobog. My family... My friends.'
'And so you chose to stay here?'
'There is nowhere in Ursus for me.'
'Sonya and Lada need me too.'
'And... I'm still very young.'
'I'm still very weak.'
'Perhaps one day, I will be able to go back to Ursus to help even more people there.'
'Perhaps one day, I will be powerful enough to make Ursus a better place.'
'And it won't just be me. There will be a great many people who will go back to Ursus, to go back home.'
'Does this... sound childish to you?'
'No, Anna.'
'Your ambitions are noble.'
'No one would dare to mock such noble ambitions.'
'If you will one day return to Ursus to make them come true...'
'I look forward to that day.'
'Thank you, Mr. Alexsandr...'
'Thank you...'
uniequip_002_ghost:
Specter clutches the candle holder tight. She remembers it. But it should not be here.
The Medical Department operators visited her a moment ago. They pricked an ever-so-cautious drop of blood from her finger, then left her alone to recite prayer from her heart, liturgical meanings discerned by none. They tend to her body, attempt to heal her rended ego—they would not bestow her such a vile gift as this.
She touches the candlelight, but the fingertip feels no hint of warmth. A momentary lucidity and tranquility race ashore like foam. The edges of the waves wash over her throat cut wide open, and zealotry, scorched sun-dry in darkness, extinguishes its bellows. In the same moment, white flame climbs her wrist, sets her nun's habit alight, and leaps from her shoulder to sink into her sweeping hair.
Through the candlelight, she looks within. Laurentina stands before a statue. The Stygian sea encases a dome teeming with lights. The figure freed from raw stone lingers in her eyes, and its shadow chisels out an alcove. There, Laurentina lifts a machine to cut stone, a 'Little Handy' roving in circles beside her, swallowing up the fragments that pitter-patter against the floor.
Through the candlelight, she looks within. Rallying cries. Piercing whistles and sawblades all around as far as the eye can see, gristle and blood peeled from body, bones met together and fractured apart. The hunters born beneath domes are tearing apart the barriers of flesh now before them, their enemies falling to the seafloor as raindrops to the surface. A lance severs open a cavity; an incisive and clarion order; amidst ocean's currents Laurentina charges in. She hears singing.
Through the candlelight, she looks within. The statue behind the candle holder is virgin holy white, and when it weeps, it casts a shadow. She is sliced apart, to then be mended; sliced apart again, to then be mended again. Finally, they use Specter to slice apart Laurentina, and allow the seeds of dry land to root within her body. Thus, the sister kneels before the candle holder, grips her pendant tight, recites prayer from her heart, liturgical meanings discerned by none.
Through the candlelight, she looks within. The door to the treatment ward is pulled open. A familiar scent. A lithe yet firm echo of footsteps strikes down the candle holder, melting it into the lights of the corridor. Specter curls up, dreaming a peaceful dream so rare for her. In her dream, she burns atop the candle holder, as if she is its fourth flame.
uniequip_002_broca:
In a gloomy jail cell, not one glimmer of light hangs about. Behind the bars, a respectably dressed gentiluomo wrinkles his brow in revulsion. In a shadowy corner sits a loud-mouthed man.
'Signore, you got any bros?'
Hearing him utter that specific word, 'bros,' the gentiluomo haughtily pulls at his sleeve collars, and speaks boastfully.
'My elder brother Davis, Signore Davis to you, is an important man in the Eastern region. He has many a means up his sleeve. I won't be loitering in here for long.'
'Nice, nice. I've got a buddy too. Bet you he's also trying every trick to get me out.'
'My brother has a lawyer who charges four thousand an hour. What does your 'bro' have?'
'A giant drill? Plus some insanely buff arms. No joke, chiseled like a rock.'
'Oh? And how is he going to rescue you from this place? Punching a hole in the wall?'
'Haha, yeah, that's just his style.'
Letting out a disdainful sneer, the gentiluomo folds his arms and silently mocks this man in his head—
'Doesn't he know the walls here are half a meter of cement? What an utter dunce.'
The door creaks open, and in comes a man carrying paperwork, his leather shoes gleaming unusually brightly in the dim of the cell.
'Signore Hengel, my pleasure. I'm your brother's attorney.'
The gentiluomo pats off his suit and gingerly stands.
'Are you here to let me out?'
'Sincere apologies, Signore Hengel, but I cannot.
'Your brother wanted me to deliver you a message: 'Enjoying the benefits of the famiglia comes with a duty to the famiglia.''
At these words, the gentiluomo's eyes grow wide.
'But it was my brother who had me do those things...'
Yet the lawyer gives him not even another glance, merely a parting remark as he turns to leave.
'Brothers must help each other out, no, signore?'
'Stop, wait, come back! You bastard!'
The gentiluomo clutches at the bars and begins to wail. The man in the corner attempts, at least, to comfort him.
'Maybe you can come with us.'
'Pull your head out. Your 'bro' isn't coming.
'Everyone who lands in here, without exception, is someone their famiglia cast away.'
'...Famiglia? It ain't anything like that. He's a buddy to me. He'll come.'
'Enough, you moron. Even setting aside how heavy the guard is out there, this wall alone is fifty whole—'
An earsplitting drilling noise cuts off the gentiluomo mid-sentence. Through the wall steadily pokes out a gargantuan drill, wrecking the concrete at such speed it may as well be shredded paper.
Dust and debris is thrown down in spades, and the ground itself lightly trembles.
A burly man steps through the yawning hole, toting the giant drill by hand. The light shining in from behind him hides his face in chiaroscuro.
Casually turning off his handheld titan, the man turns to ask something to the dumbstruck gentiluomo.
'Are you coming with us, signore?'
uniequip_002_fuze:
'Buddy, you are NOT a chatty type, huh!'
After the gazillionth attempt to start up a conversation without getting a reaction, the Cautus worker in a yellow pair-o'-ears helmet stops operating his control panel and gives the man beside him a pat on the shoulders. With the machine kicked into auto anyway, it's not like it needs nannying.
Seeming to recognize as much, the man finally turns his head. His eyes are hidden behind a black visor, barely discernible. He remains silent, and simply extends two fingers on his right hand and gives his own helmet a few taps.
'Go on and say somethin', will ya? Saaaaay—woooords—'
Throughout this temporary worksite echoes the rumble of Originium electronics, more often than not a soundboard to rival a nomadic plate's engine layer. But the voicebox of a Rim Billy worker, like the workers themselves, is filled with a power that cuts through just about everything.
The man appears a little confused. He feels around behind him, then unexpectedly pulls out a mirror. He takes a glance at his own reflection, then raps on his helmet again in the same manner as before.
The worker doesn't get to respond before he sees, out of nowhere on the man's visor, a smiley face positioned right between where his eyes would be. There's a line of Victorian text below too, split by his nose into halves. The left side reads 'I'M SHY,' and the right, 'AND QUIET.'
The worker tries as hard as he can to keep a straight face. His lower lip twitches side to side, his teeth grind over each other, and he doesn't leak a single word.
But soon, he can't hold in anymore, snorts, and begins to laugh.
'Probe has reached scheduled depth. Drill decelerating. Prepare to turn off and take samples.'
That's an announcement from Control Center 2. It sits 80m straight above them, and 50m above that are the natural caves of Camp 2 and tracks to the auxiliary shafts. Another 600m up is the surface, and outside from there are the Targangils Mountains for miles and miles forever.
The drill mentioned in the announcement is a fair way deeper into the earth than they are.
'—Hold on, Number 2 is too deep. Abnormal tremors in 2's shaft walls. Calling emergency stop!' The second announcement comes hot on the heels of the first, as if some kind of prank.
Something unwelcome has been welcomed. The worker throws himself onto the control panel, pounding a fist on the largest, roundest red button of them all. It's the one to emergency-dump the drill and inject extra polymer prep into the shaft walls.
But the injector doesn't respond, and the Originium electronics continue to roar.
A ginormous thud echoes through the worksite, seemingly not from deeper depths, but from times long, long ago.
One thud becomes two, then three, then a string of them. The two watch as even the wall outside them finally begins to experience its own fierce tremors.
Number 2 has drilled too deep and awakened something, and that something is heading for the sunlight.
'Detonating all Cluster Charges!' The worker's never heard this voice before, but in an instant discerns that it has to be the man's shout.
Perhaps because of this shout, or perhaps because of what it triggers elsewhere...
The tremors cease. Silence seems to reign again for a while, until there comes another announcement urging evacuation.
'Your tender said 'use of Originium explosives forbidden', so here I am.'
This may be the second time the man's opened his mouth today, and his voice is far quieter than a moment ago.
'There's issues with your emergency injector system. Once we're up top, come with me to tell them, and then I'll take a look.'
'Er. Right. You got it.'
After experiencing an accident whose true severity will only be known later, a conversation finally ensues.
'...What's with that light-up stuff in your visor though, eh? That's one hell of a lark, buddy.'
uniequip_002_varkis:
The sky isn't dark yet, but he begins to set up camp. There is no need to rush, he tells himself.
He has resigned from his ferryman job, even though the citizens of Athenius voted to have him stay. With his apprentice gone, he no longer has any time-sensitive responsibilities on his shoulders.
This freedom terrifies him and he knows it: he's slowing down. Compared to when he left his homeland five years ago, the land seems no different now—desolate and quiet. The clearly depicted river on the tattered map in his hand was gone without a trace.
The priest said that snowmelt will eventually form new rivers, but all he sees now is desolation.
An indistinct fear creeps into his heart once more, an emotion he has long been acquainted with. Ever since he embarked on this journey home, when he arrived in Athenius with Ithakos's blood-soaked robes and stayed after the priest invited him to, he had been caught in its clutches. It was the fear that kept him there with no way to return home, that had him unleash his rage and hatred upon the Sargonians. What can he even do if he goes home and realizes the past is gone forever? What else can he chase after?
By now the sky is completely dark. He lowers his oar and retrieves the lantern hanging on it. Old and riddled with signs of wear, yet it follows him everywhere. It used to be an ordinary oil lamp, but Ithakos had modified it to run on Originium and added a windproof case designed with latches that could be easily opened for a soft light to guide him home. He still remembers that night. He was adding notes to the river map based on his observations, as Ithakos hammered away on his workbench nearby to improve the lantern.
Finally, he works up a slight smile as he carefully wipes the dirt off the lantern and tries to open the case—but fails to.
It is stuck. This has never happened before. He dares not use force, nor does he know how to repair it, so he can only gently turn it over. Cold sweat forms beneath his mask and on his back as fear returns. After leaving Ithakos's armor and Arts Unit to the guerillas and leaving his bloody chiton to Athenius, this is the last item he owns with any connection to him. If he loses even this, then what should he—
Click.
The lantern opens up.
A thin fiber falls out of it.
He breathes a sigh of relief as he raises the lantern to the river map. After a long silence, he remembers to look at the fiber, surprising himself when he realizes it is the top of a reed. Perhaps the wind blew it over the night before, or in the morning, and he only now noticed its presence.
Just as he only now realizes how soft the black earth is beneath him—though the rivers have yet to return, the annelids in the soil were already weaving through the ground in his absence, and the reeds of the rivers and marshes are once again regaining their moisture.
At daybreak he can go even further, he thinks.
uniequip_002_astesi:
'According to the most recent 'Startide freeze' calculations, these two stars have changed phases. But you still believe disaster is headed our way. Why is that?'
'Hey, where'd you even come from, girlie? How am I supposed to sell these bracelets if I don't say that? Are you interested in astrology too? You seem like you come from a well-to-do family... Why don't I help you read the stars?'
'Astrology is a complicated subject with a long history. Father said I wouldn't be able to understand the sky's appearance if I couldn't comprehend the ancient records, let alone read it.'
'Hahaha. Don't break your brain with all that studying, my young friend.
'Why don't you tell me, what's the point of reading the stars if not to give people empty comfort?'
......
'I'd like to resolve all your doubts in my father's stead, dear reporters.'
Francois Urbica is surrounded by reporters. They had failed to secure the rights to interview Rhine Lab personnel, so now they turn their resentment into ridicule towards the Astrological Research Association. A quiet Liberi girl walks up to them, and Francois raises an eyebrow, but does not stop her.
'Astrology embodies humanity's earliest interest in the sky. When the first astrology study was published, aircraft had yet to leap into our skies, and Columbia wasn't even born yet. Scholars across generations have observed the starry sky day after day, and after every Startide, they would gather and process the complex data they received, overturning conclusions. There was only one thing keeping them going: the belief that our lives were entwined with the distant stars.
'With today's technology, we can identify many errors in their past writings, but be it from the perspective of an astrologist or a historian, their meticulous records are still an incredible achievement. Perhaps we now believe that such ancient theories should be put to rest, but the hole above Trimounts is not the truth itself—it is a door we can all peek into. As a bibliography consultant for Rhine Lab, I know well that, be it through shared experience or objective inference, Casters of astrology and scholars of astronomy have always shared the same goal. It would be unfortunate to abandon our predecessors' research. If astrology says we can never truly understand the stars, then as a scholar, I will continue our search through the scientific method. But if there comes a day when science also fails to grasp the secrets that lie outside the dome, astrology may yet offer us a new possibility.'
......
'Is there something on my face, Elena?'
'Do you still remember, Sia? When we were kids, you met a famous peddler who used astrology to swindle people. He made you so mad you cried all the way home. No one could get you to stop.'
'*sigh* Are you here to laugh at me, then?'
'No! I just meant, if it were the you from today, you'd have been able to shut that scammer up. Just like you shut up all those reporters earlier. I used to be a bit worried you'd be stuck under Father's influence if you kept studying the stars, but now I know I have nothing to worry about—
'You were so cool just now, Sia!'
uniequip_002_sidero:
'Thou shalt love Corinia.' Thus reads the inscription that crowns the stone pillar marking the city's gate. Its carver must have pictured that all those departing the city would read it the moment they lifted their heads. Now, though, stallkeeps and mercenaries throng the gate as tightly as packed fins, and those who look up will see nothing but smoke-stained graffiti and billboards. These used to be Sideroca's stomping grounds as a child—she'd watch aging mercs grumble as they waited to find employers, snippets of their words helping her piece together a map in her head—the map she'd use for her escape plan one day.
It's been years since then. She's returned, here beneath this gate once more. The branch director who'd referred Sideroca to Rhodes Island is here with her now, touring the old haunt together and talking about old times. The director confesses that back then, more than anything, she'd rushed to sign up Sideroca because she didn't want to let a talent like her go anywhere else. Sideroca had that little something extra compared to your average drifter. Real recognizes real, so to speak.
A freight boat needs a ballast to sail, and the wandering mercs and merchants of this citadel need something spiritual to weigh down their legs, lest they be trapped behind the mountains. Sideroca was barely an adult when she found her legs, firmer ones than any merc drowning their life away in booze. So what did keep her so rock-steady?
She doesn't have an answer right away. She scrutinizes Corinia once more, this city built on the idea of an eye for an eye. She can't stand the place in all its dark, bloodied glory. It sickens her how the books you learn to read from here teach you all the different names of money. She despises how children play pretend by copying the way grown-ups haggle and bargain and use each other for their own gain. To her, Corinia is one giant example of what things shouldn't be. With every step, she's reminding herself: don't end up like this. Don't end up like the merchants who peddle fakes beneath the gate, or the mercs who cry ripoff and smash their stalls up.
A crude rock can be carved into pillar decorations or boat ballasts. Yet, if you price it as a jewel and cling to it, you'll waste all your energy and sink to the river's bottom with it. The further Sideroca travels from her homeland, the more clearly she understands this and many other things.
She has no interest in entering the city itself. Just as she's about to go, the branch director asks if she's ever seen how that inscription has a second half:
'For thy countless paths begin from here.'
uniequip_002_akafyu:
Kirara glances at Akafuyu sitting in front of the TV.
'Why are you suddenly so interested in this thing? You've been stealing looks at it.' Akafuyu doesn't turn around, but simply removes a shoulder guard with one hand and tosses it to Kirara. Her eyesight may be poor, but she's so aware of her surroundings, she might as well have a camera in her back.
'This armor...'
'It's an heirloom. It's not valuable. My master doesn't go out to fight much, so it was bequeathed to me.'
'Um, the design...'
'It's a very special shape to the armor. In the old days, each family had its own style.'
Kirara touches the shoulder guard and compares it to the armor in her game. She starts to think the developers must know of Akafuyu.

Why do people like to drink?
When Rafaela first began her bartending job, the question floated to her mind from time to time.
She can always ask her papá when she has a question. But this is a work thing—Papá usually barely talks to her about his work, so likewise, she'd better not ask him about hers.
And she doesn't want to ask her hermano about it.
Especially not her hermano.
So she'll ask a customer! People are always coming and going in Dossoles, but in just a short time, Rafaela's learned to recognize a lot of regulars, and they all like to talk to her.
According to the person dancing wildly to the jota while calling her 'Rafa' and 'chica' at the top of their lungs, you drink for the color, the mouthfeel, the taste, and for a moment of joy.
But according to the person calling her 'Señorita Silva' while leaning on the bar counter, sluggishly lifting a hand as they sing fado, you drink just to forget and be free from your worries for a while.
'Thanks for asking,' they add more often than not.
Rafaela isn't sure if she comprehended all these answers, but she makes sure to remember every one. It's how it should be, she thinks.
Times change.
As the landship sails, there's a regular thrumming all throughout the hold. Rafaela hasn't gotten used to this noise yet—after all, it's nothing like fowlbeast chirps or beating waves—but she doesn't react badly to it at all.
She's asked another operator before, and now she knows this is how it should be on the ship.
In the landship, music is more varied too, with lots she's never heard before.
Even so, the person who dances wildly while calling her 'Rafa' and 'chica' at the top of their lungs is still there. When she meets this kind of person, she does as they request, and squeezes some of the sweetest fruit juice into their drinks, adding some of the most bracing syrup. But at the same time, she secretly dilutes these flavors until they make for the coolest, most reinvigorating flavors. She gives whoever's drinking it a moment of joy, and all the wake-up they need to bask in that joy.
And there's still the person who calls her 'Señorita Silva' and 'Miss La Pluma' while leaning on the bar counter, sluggishly lifting a hand. When she meets this kind of person, she does as they quietly ask her, and pulls the strongest, most biting bottles from the racks to pour into their glass. But at the same time, she doesn't forget to mix in a little of the finest pedigree, sourced locally from Logroño. She watches them down a glass of bitter drink, but knows the taste left behind won't be totally astringent.
'Thank you,' they say in approval more often than not. Sometimes she nods, but feels strange about it, so other times she just doesn't nod at all.
Of course, this method of mixology isn't entirely described in the Dossoles Guide to Cocktails, but she makes a note of it in there herself.
And she's already given the book away to someone who deserves it. She may not have it anymore, but she's learned it by heart.
Rafaela feels that this way is good.
This is how it should be.

This is not the first time I bring you out to sea. You've heard countless ocean tales from me.
You already know how the tides flow, and how they ebb. You know that when pale blue light shines in the surface, you are no longer to bother the fins and seabeasts. You know that when the pinnacle of Oberos Lighthouse touches the very top of the Shadow-Moon, we Ægir should return home.
You are familiar with the skyscraping surges, and the smallest of sprays. You've learned to converse with them, haven't you? You love to chatter with them, and they are glad to tell you how they are feeling. Do you still remember what they told you? They are but one part of the sea; they are one and the same. You know where the surges will stop and rest, and you know where the tiniest suds will assimilate into the ocean. I have nothing left to tell you now. Hence, this time will be very different; you must prepare yourself, and you must listen to me.
We are familiar with the earth and ocean; they have made me and my vessel old, unable to reach farther places. You see? The briny winds dry my cheeks, the air erodes at my bones, the starlight presses down on my shoulders, and if not for you, even lifting this oar would likely be beyond me. But you are different. Your arms are still growing, your bones and flesh are sturdier than mine, your eyes livelier, and your thoughts brighter. You should make it to higher, farther waters. Young child, you must sail far. Child, this sea will be very different. Gone will be the fins you know, gone will be the fearsome seabeasts, and there will be no lighthouse to guide your way, as your destination is in the seas beyond where the stars shine... However, still there will be tides there, still there will be waves, and still there will be countless glimmering specks of ocean foam just like you, Highmore. I trust that, just as before, you will be familiar with these new tides, and familiar with these new waves. They will tell you stories even I haven't heard. You must accompany the twin moons—no, you must go somewhere higher, farther, vaster than the twin moons...
The meaning of a voyage is not mine to give, for you will find it yourself. But first you must remember, Highmore, remember what I've told you. A voyage is by no means a retreat, and the reason we leave our home is by no means our disappointment with it. Your voyage is because you are young, because you are sturdy, and because it is for a home as young and hope-filled as you. Once you have seen tide upon tide, seen wave upon wave, you must return home, and you must return to tell us.
Highmore, a voyage is not a farewell. You must remember, remember your anchor, for so long as you have your anchor, your vessel will be sure to make landfall; so long as you have your anchor, you, voyaging child, will be sure to return home.

Ernesto's face also bears a cheerful smile, and he raises a glass to meet the other.
The communication terminal buzzes. Ernesto silently glances down at the screen, and leaks a slight frown.
But soon he returns to his previously nonchalant look, as if nothing had happened, and begins introducing the room's decorations to Charles. Afterwards, as Charles appreciates the art on display, Ernesto deftly sweeps a hand over his guest's wine glass, sprinkling a transparent powder into the drink.

'Mr. Charles isn't used to the climate here in Dossoles, so I believe he won't be able to perform on stage today.'

'He should recover by tomorrow, I'll take his place later this afternoon.' Ernesto pats the bodyguard on the shoulder to assure him.
He does not wait for him to respond before leaving.
Returning to his room, Ernesto opens a suitcase lying quietly in a corner. The bottom compartment contains various documents and office stationery he usually uses—all neatly arranged and normal-looking—until he opens a hidden compartment filled with weapons.

'Enough, Ernesto. You're the one who decided to give yourself so much trouble.' As he speaks, he picks up the microphone next to him. 'The audience at least is innocent, so let them enjoy themselves.'
